title: Alex Cooper Poised to Drop UTA After Tough Period of Media Scrutiny
description:
Alex Cooper seems intent on unraveling some of the current relationships that have helped underpin her production company, Unwell.

	The star podcas
body:
Alex Cooper seems intent on unraveling some of the current relationships that have helped underpin her production company, Unwell.

	The star podcaster and media entrepreneur is poised to drop her current talent agency, UTA, according to a person familiar with the matter, frustrated in part by its continuing relationships with Alix Earle and Dave Portnoy, two prominent influencers and podcasters who have feuded with her. Cooper last week shut down a beverage venture, Unwell Beverage Co., which was launched last year with Nestle SA as a partner, according to a report from Bloomberg.
	

	 UTA has helped Cooper build and scale her company, Unwell, and over the years has helped broker deals that had her host interviews for Peacock during NBCUniversal’s coverage of the 2024 Paris Olympics, and launch her Unwell Network, a platform for other creators and influencers.


	UTA declined to make executives available for comment. 

	A shift in representation would come after Unwell,  which Cooper founded with her husband, Matt Kaplan, landed its first outside investor: Patrick Whitesell, co-founder of WME and former executive chairman of successor company Endeavor. Whitesell’s WTSL, an investment firm focused on media, entertainment and sports he launched after exiting Endeavor and WME last year, has invested an undisclosed sum in Unwell that values the business at $500 million, according to information released August 12 by Unwell. Cooper and Kaplan, who self-funded the company targeting Gen Z women audiences, retain a majority ownership stake. Formed in 2023, Unwell says it has been profitable from day one and sees the WTSL investment as growth capital.
	

	Unwell said that in addition to the funding, WTSL would bring “deep strategic expertise, industry relationships and a proven track record of supporting some of the most innovative companies and storytellers in media,” including Peyton Manning’s Omaha Productions.

	“Alex, Matt and the team have demonstrated an exceptional ability to anticipate where audiences are headed and create entertainment experiences that resonate deeply,” Whitesell said last week. “The company’s growth, audience connection and cultural relevance set it apart, and we believe Unwell is uniquely positioned to help define the present and future of media.”

	Whitesell’s funding followed a pair of recent exposés alleging behind-the-scenes chaos at Unwell. According to a Vanity Fair story in June, one Unwell freelancer alleged that Kaplan “creates the most toxic work environment that I’ve ever seen”; anonymous sources also said Kaplan had questioned employees about their sex lives and commented on their physical appearance. In April, Bloomberg reported that Kaplan “has earned a reputation for frequently yelling at staff members” and said Unwell’s employees were “looking for the exit.”

	Cooper, in an interview at Cannes Lions this June with the Wall Street Journal, was asked about the allegations. “I will just kind of leave it at ‘Don’t believe everything that you read on the internet’ — but I think everyone knows that at this point,” she said. Cooper also said, “I think that we have done a really incredible job at Unwell, and I think if you walk the halls, there are so many people that are so happy to work at this company. … I think, unfortunately, being a woman in this industry is extremely difficult because you’re held to a completely different standard. Whether it’s a smear campaign being created for someone’s narrative, whatever it be.”

	Earle, a podcaster and influencer, gained some her greatest fame while hosting the podcast “Hot Mess,” which was produced by Unwell. Dave Portnoy, the founder of Barstool Sports, alleged in a memoir that Cooper and her former co-host, Sofia Franklyn, planned to say they were harassed in order to get out of a previous contract with Barstool, which helped launch “Call Her Daddy.”
	

	–Todd Spangler contributed to this story

schema.headline: Alex Cooper Poised to Drop UTA After Tough Period of Media Scrutiny

title: ‘The Challenge’ Contestants Pay Tribute to Tyler Duckworth: ‘You Were the Brother I Never Had’
description: “The Challenge” two-time winner Tyler Duckworth died Tuesday in North Dakota, and his fellow contestants are remembering him as a “joy to be around”
body:
“The Challenge” two-time winner Tyler Duckworth died Tuesday in North Dakota, and his fellow contestants are remembering him as a “joy to be around” with “vibrant energy.”

	Johnny “Bananas” Devenanzio posted a video tribute to Duckworth on Instagram on Sunday. The pair started their reality show careers together in their early 20s on “The Real World: Key West” in 2006. Devenanzio and Duckworth also competed together and won “The Challenge: Rivals” in 2011. 
	

	“You were more than a friend. More than a roommate,” Devenanzio wrote in the caption of the post. “You were the brother I never had. Rest easy, Tyler. You’ll always be family.”


	Brad Fiorenza wrote, “So grateful we got to see him on this day. Thoughts and prayers to his family. May his amazing soul live on forever in the lives he touched 🕊️RIP Tyler.”

	Derrick Kosinski, who competed on the show and co-hosted the “Challenge Mania” podcast, told People Magazine, “We shared a room on ‘All Stars 2’ and he was an amazing human being. His passing is so sad. He was always such a bright light and incredible joy to be around. He also kicked my ass in elimination on the original ‘Cutthroat.’ And that was after he eliminated Johnny Bananas in the famous Bananas backpack elimination, ‘Back Up Off Me.’ He went toe to toe with CT for 40 minutes! He doesn’t get his flowers often enough for that. And he won that season. And then won again with Johnny on ‘Rivals.’”

	Tina Barta, a contestant from “Road Rules: South Pacific” and multiple seasons of “The Challenge,” wrote, “We shared an experience that very few people will ever fully understand, and somewhere along the way, it became more than a show or an adventure. It became friendship. It became history. It became family.”

schema.headline: ‘The Challenge’ Contestants Pay Tribute to Tyler Duckworth: ‘You Were the Brother I Never Had’

title: Stray Kids Score Their Biggest Sales Week as ‘This & That’ Debuts Atop Albums Chart
description:
Stray Kids have scored their biggest sales week yet as their latest, “This & That,” becomes their ninth No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

	The group bows
body:
Stray Kids have scored their biggest sales week yet as their latest, “This & That,” becomes their ninth No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

	The group bows atop the chart with 369,000 equivalent album units, with traditional album sales accounting for 357,000 of that sum. The latest feat extends their record for most No. 1s among groups this century, tying them with the Rolling Stones for second-most No. 1s in the chart’s history among groups, only behind the Beatles with 19 No. 1s. Additionally, “This & That” has the sixth-largest week for an album in 2026 and second-largest by traditional album sales behind the debut of BTS’ “Arirang” in March with 532,000.
	

	Stray Kids previously earned their first No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with “Oddinary” in 2022. Two years later, they became the first act to debut their first six entries at the top spot following the release of “Hop.”


	Elsewhere, Ariana Grande‘s “Petal” drops from No. 1 to 2 in its second week, earning 82,000 equivalent album units. Olivia Rodrigo’s “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love” holds steady at No. 3, followed by Ella Langley’s “Dandelion” at No. 4 and Morgan Wallen’s “I’m the Problem,” which dips from No. 2 to 5.

	Rounding out the rest of the top 10 are Noah Kahan’s “The Great Divide,” followed by the debut of Pooh Shiesty’s “All Eyes on Shiest” at No. 7. Karol G’s latest album, “No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto,” bows at No. 8, while Drake’s “Iceman” slides from No. 6 to 9. Role Model’s latest album, “Chuck Timely & the Hourglass,” bows at No. 10 with 38,500 equivalent album units.

schema.headline: Stray Kids Score Their Biggest Sales Week as ‘This & That’ Debuts Atop Albums Chart

title: ‘I Don’t Know’: Kenneth Branagh on Directing,  ‘Harry Potter’ and How Christopher Nolan Had Him Speaking Russian Backwards
description: Sunday at the Edinburgh Intl. Film Festival turned into Edinbranagh, with a morning screening of the four-hour epic “Hamlet” followed by a wide-rang
body:
Sunday at the Edinburgh Intl. Film Festival turned into Edinbranagh, with a morning screening of the four-hour epic “Hamlet” followed by a wide-ranging onstage conversation with Kenneth Branagh, which began with him receiving the inaugural EIFF Outstanding Contribution to Cinema award.

	“Festivals are more important to our industry than ever before,” Branagh said, holding the award and arguing they offer a lifeline to films struggling to find a traditional theatrical path. He promptly turned the honor back on the packed audience: “You are the reason, certainly the reason why I stand here.”
	

	Hosted by Guardian critic Peter Bradshaw, the talk jumped across Branagh’s sprawling career.


	He recalled preparing his 1991 thriller “Dead Again” from Sydney Pollack’s office when he felt the room move. Then Pollack’s Academy Awards started sliding.

	“I started to see the two Oscars do a sort of dance on the top shelf,” Branagh said. “It was an earthquake.”

	“Dead Again,” his neo-noir follow up to “Henry V,” had its own shaky beginnings. Early previews were “disastrous,” with audiences heading for the exits. The fix? Restore screenwriter Scott Frank’s original idea of rendering the past in black and white. “Suddenly the preview score went through the roof,” Branagh said. “We were loved again by our studio family.”

	Christopher Nolan offered a different kind of ordeal. On “Tenet,” Branagh asked whether his Russian oligarch should speak Russian backwards while moving backwards through time.

	“I saw this terrible, dangerous light in his eye,” he recalled. Nolan’s answer: “Yes, I think you would.”
	

	So Branagh spent lunch learning backwards Russian.

	Then came Hogwarts.

	Branagh had assumed Gilderoy Lockhart in “Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets” might mean three or four weeks’ work. Instead, “I was on it for nine months.” The crew list, he said, was “the size of a telephone directory.”

	On his first day, Branagh thought he saw Daniel Radcliffe and Rupert Grint, only to discover stunt doubles and stand-ins filling an entire classroom while the young stars were at school. When the real actors appeared, Hogwarts had become its own ecosystem: “Notes were being passed. Little darts were being thrown at people.”

	For Branagh, the scale was staggering, children essentially living inside a fictional school while surrounded by “the entire British film industry.”

	The conversation kept circling back to Shakespeare. Branagh said his early theater company had a “missionary zeal” to make the plays feel immediate rather than bogged down by reverence. He wanted his parents to be able to watch Shakespeare “and not feel they had to read the play beforehand.”

	“When Shakespeare was real, there was nothing in the way,” he said. “You just had truth. If it was truthful, you felt it, you understood it.

	That instinct fuelled his directorial debut “Henry V,” made despite producer David Puttnam’s late warning that the film could collapse and damage Branagh’s career, a sentiment Puttnam later retracted in a gracious note of apology. Branagh said one of the most useful lessons he learned as a director could be summed up in three words: “I don’t know.”

	The afternoon’s most personal moment came with “Belfast.” Written during the pandemic, the semi-autobiographical film emerged, Branagh said, after the story had sat inside him for roughly 40 years.

	His sister’s reaction to the script: “My God, for a very private man, you’ve really put it all out there now, haven’t you?”

	Branagh grew emotional.

	“It was cathartic,” he said. “It was necessary. Somehow it was necessary.”

	After a career spanning Shakespeare, superheroes, Poirot, Hogwarts and Hollywood, his closing advice to an audience member was simple:

	“Keep practising and enjoy.”

schema.headline: ‘I Don’t Know’: Kenneth Branagh on Directing,  ‘Harry Potter’ and How Christopher Nolan Had Him Speaking Russian Backwards

title: Mariska Hargitay Says Jalen Brunson Is ‘Definitely’ Getting a Role in ‘Law & Order: Special Victims Unit’: ‘It’s Happening’
description: Mariska Hargitay told Variety at the HBO Max Emmy Nominee Celebration that New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson is “definitely” getting a role in “Law
body:
Mariska Hargitay told Variety at the HBO Max Emmy Nominee Celebration that New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson is “definitely” getting a role in “Law and Order: Special Victims Unit.”

	“It’s definitely happening,” Hargitay said. “He’s kind of magnificent that way. He is just open and ready. I don’t think there is much Jalen can’t do.”


	When asked if she wants to help Brunson get an Emmy nomination on top of his recent NBA championship, Hargitay said. “I do! I don’t think he can handle any more awards, to be honest. Right now, I think he’s like, ‘Give me a rest.’”
	

	Brunson’s role on the long-running NBC procedural has been teased since the moment he stepped off the court after his championship win against the San Antonio Spurs in June. When a reporter asked what he planned to do in the offseason, Brunson said, “Try to get on ‘SVU.’”


	Hargitay has likewise been dropping hints that the Knicks star will soon join the show. During an appearance on “Today,” she said of Brunson’s role, “I’m hoping that we might — don’t tell anyone, but — see him on SVU.’” She added, “We’ve got some things in the works.”

	In an interview with TMZ Sports, former “SVU” star Christopher Meloni said Brunson “absolutely” has what it takes to get a role on the show.

	“I don’t know if you’ve heard, but he’s the world champion,” Meloni said. “He can do whatever the hell he wants.” He then added, “He’s got the force of will.”

schema.headline: Mariska Hargitay Says Jalen Brunson Is ‘Definitely’ Getting a Role in ‘Law & Order: Special Victims Unit’: ‘It’s Happening’

title: Dolly Parton Skips Dollywood Ride Opening Amid Ongoing Health Problems: ‘My Nashville Doctor Has Kinda Clipped My Wings’
description:
Dolly Parton was unable to attend the opening of NightFlight Expedition at Dollywood on Friday due to ongoing “health issues.”

	Dollywood President
body:
Dolly Parton was unable to attend the opening of NightFlight Expedition at Dollywood on Friday due to ongoing “health issues.”

	Dollywood President Eugene Naughton shared a pre-recorded video of the singer during the dedication ceremony for the new ride. “Well, hey Eugene. I’m right here… Well, kind of. Sorta,” Parton said in the video. “I’m still in Nashville, and I’m sorry about that. I was supposed to be there in person like I planned.”
	

	Parton shared that she had been feeling dizzy and dehydrated. She told fans her doctor had advised her against traveling to the opening. “My Nashville doctor has kinda clipped my wings, saying, ‘You ain’t traveling this week.’ So I guess, if your doctor tells you, ‘you ain’t traveling this week,’ you ain’t traveling this week,” she said.


	“You have fun, and I’m gonna see you down the road,” she added.

	In May, Parton canceled her Las Vegas residency, which had been rescheduled for September. She was originally slated to perform six shows at Caesars Palace in December 2025, but postponed the shows due to “health challenges.”

	Parton gave the keynote address at Dollywood during the 41st anniversary celebration in March, one of her first major appearances since the health scare.

	Parton bought an interest in the theme park in 1986, and it was renamed to Dollywood. The Dollywood Company operates the theme park, a dinner theater, Dolly Parton’s Stampede, Dollywood’s Splash Country waterpark and the Dream More Resort and Spa. Located in the Knoxville metropolitan area, it is now the biggest ticketed tourist attraction in Tennessee.

schema.headline: Dolly Parton Skips Dollywood Ride Opening Amid Ongoing Health Problems: ‘My Nashville Doctor Has Kinda Clipped My Wings’

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Hits $2 Billion Worldwide in Three Weeks
description:
New day, new box office milestone for Sony’s latest Spidey adventure. 

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has surpassed $2 billion in global ticket sales
body:
New day, new box office milestone for Sony’s latest Spidey adventure. 

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has surpassed $2 billion in global ticket sales, eclipsing the rare benchmark after just three weekends of release. The comic book adventure, starring Tom Holland as Marvel‘s neighborhood web-slinger, has grossed $785 million in North America and $1.23 billion overseas for a grand total of $2.022 billion.


	The newest “Spider-Man” is one of eight films in history to reach the $2 billion club, joining the small-but-mighty company of 2009’s “Avatar” ($2.9 billion), 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.7 billion), 2022’s “Avatar: The Way of Water” ($2.3 billion), 1994’s “Titanic” ($2.2 billion), 2015’s “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” ($2.07 billion) and 2018’s “Avengers: Infinity War” ($2.03 billion). (Meanwhile, the prior “Spider-Man” installment, 2021’s “No Way Home,” was this close with $1.9 billion but missed the milestone because the superhero adventure didn’t play in China.) Notably, “Brand New Day” is the second-fastest film to reach the threshold after “Endgame,” which got there after 11 days.
	

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has been shattering expectations since landing in theaters at the end of July. The movie, Holland’s fourth solo outing as Peter Parker, captured a record-setting $355 million in North America and a staggering $932 million globally in its opening weekend and then cleared $1 billion after just six days of release.

	There’s no question that “Brand New Day” will leave the big screen as one of the highest-grossing movies of all time (in fact, it’s already the eighth-biggest worldwide release ever). But where will ticket sales ultimately wind up? With stratospheric enthusiasm and encouraging staying power, box office watchers are wondering whether “Brand New Day” could become the only movie to ever reach $1 billion domestically (“Star Wars: The Force Awakens” currently stands as the biggest North American release ever with $936 million) and maybe… possibly… potentially even the first to hit $3 billion globally.

schema.headline: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Hits $2 Billion Worldwide in Three Weeks

title: ‘The Sopranos’ Star Drea de Matteo Says Starting an OnlyFans Was a ‘Political Statement’: ‘F— You. I Don’t Have to Work’
description: “The Sopranos” star Drea de Matteo recently told Jamie Kennedy on the “Hate to Break It To Ya” podcast (via EW) that starting her OnlyFans page was
body:
“The Sopranos” star Drea de Matteo recently told Jamie Kennedy on the “Hate to Break It To Ya” podcast (via EW) that starting her OnlyFans page was a “political statement.”

	“In some ways, the OnlyFans page was almost like a political statement on my part in a way…It was like, ‘Fuck you. I don’t have to work,’” de Matteo said.

	She went on to add that some critics think, because of her Emmy-winning turn as Adriana la Cerva on the HBO mob drama, that she is “made of fucking money.” However, de Matteo explained that the whole reason she started her OnlyFans was because of financial problems.
	

	“Everyone sees me coming, they’re like, ‘Here comes that rich bitch from The Sopranos,’” she said. “And it’s like, no, I’m not at all. In fact, you know, I live a pretty fucking normal life. I had to do that [OnlyFans] page to get a lien off my house after foreclosure.”

	Earlier in the interview, de Matteo said that when she first launched her OnlyFans, it was to “start a podcast because I was afraid that I’d be censored.” But after getting encouragement from her kids, she shared a photo of herself in a bikini on her page, and “within 75 minutes” she made enough to pay the lien on her house.

	In a 2024 interview with Variety, de Matteo shared how OnlyFans helped her financially during the pandemic while facing judgment from her family for not getting vaccinated. She recalled, “[During the pandemic], my brother was like, ‘You know, you’re risking everyone in your home’s life right now [by not being vaccinated].’ And then years later, when I ended up having to open up an OnlyFans page just to save my home, because nobody would help me at that time because I didn’t ‘do the right thing,’ he was like, ‘Your body, your choice. I’m with you all the way.’”

schema.headline: ‘The Sopranos’ Star Drea de Matteo Says Starting an OnlyFans Was a ‘Political Statement’: ‘F— You. I Don’t Have to Work’

title: Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Remains No. 1 With $70 Million, ‘End of Oak Street’ Debuts to $21 Million
description:
Dog days of summer? This year’s August at the box office didn’t get the memo.

	This popcorn season is ending with a bang rather than the usual whim
body:
Dog days of summer? This year’s August at the box office didn’t get the memo.

	This popcorn season is ending with a bang rather than the usual whimper as “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey” continue to pack in crowds. Meanwhile, two new movies, Warner Bros.’ prehistoric sci-fi mystery “The End of Oak Street” with Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor and Paramount’s animated sequel “PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie,” each debuted above $20 million.
	

	Despite those newcomers, “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” remained No. 1 in North America with $70 million in its third weekend of release. Sony and Marvel’s comic book epic, starring Tom Holland as Peter Parker, has been a behemoth with $785 million domestically and $2.02 billion globally to date. It’s the second-fastest film to join the $2 billion club after 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame,” which accomplished the rare feat in 11 days.


	“The Odyssey” stayed in second place with $23.2 million in its fifth weekend of release. Universal’s big-budget Greek epic has generated a staggering $504.6 million in North America and $1.29 billion worldwide to date. That’s after debuting this weekend in China to a solid $36.6 million. It’s the second-highest-grossing movie of the year after “Spider-Man” as well as director Christopher Nolan’s biggest of all time — an especially impressive feat for a drama that’s nearly three hours long and adapted from a poem that’s thousands of years old.

	Hollywood is celebrating because this summer’s office is already the biggest since “the before times,” with revenues surpassing $4 billion for only the second time since COVID. Domestic ticket sales stand at $4.24 billion from May 1 through Aug. 16, running 23% ahead of the same period in 2025 and nearly 6% ahead of 2019. There’s a chance that popcorn season even eclipses the all-time summer record set in 23 with $4.755 billion (not adjusted for inflation), according to Rentrak.
	

	“This August feels particularly notable with ‘The Odyssey’ and ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ providing blockbuster momentum,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends, Paul Dergarabedian. “The final weeks of summer could provide a historic home stretch to what has already been a remarkable summer movie season.”

	“The End of Oak Street” launched in third place to a middling $21 million from 3,446 venues. The PG-13 movie also collected $26 million overseas for a global tally of $46 million. It’s a tepid start for the $80 million-budgeted movie, so the studio will rely on positive word-of-mouth to help with staying power. However critics seemed to like “Oak Street” more than audiences; the film holds a “B” grade on CinemaScore and 84% on Rotten Tomatoes. David Robert Mitchell wrote and directed the PG-13 survival thriller, which follows a mysterious cosmic event that transports a suburban family to prehistoric times.

	“This is late summer escapist entertainment, but right now audiences are still escaping to ‘Spider-Man,'”  says David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. 

	Unless “Oak Street” rebounds, it’ll be the latest underperforming tentpole for Warner Bros. following June’s “Supergirl” and this spring’s “The Bride.” It puts pressure on the studio’s Tom Cruise-led comedy “Digger,” which opens in October and carries a substantial $130 million price tag. 

	Fourth place went to “PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie” with $20.5 million from 3,500 North American theaters. Those ticket sales are even with the studio’s prior “PAW Patrol” sequel, 2023’s “The Mighty Movie,” which ignited to $22 million and eventually climbed to $205 million globally against a $30 million budget. “The Dino Movie” carries a slightly larger $40 million price tag, which was split between Paramount and Spin Master. Overseas, the newest “PAW Patrol” has earned $48.5 million for a global tally of $69 million.

	Rounding out the top five was “Katseye: Wild Hearts,” a documentary about the girl group, with $3.8 million from just 724 screens. 

	Fittingly, “Six: The Musical Live” debuted in sixth place with $3 million from 1,462 locations. It’s a filmed version of the popular Broadway show, and initial returns are similar to other recent live-captures like “Waitress: The Musical ($2.6 million) and “Merrily We Roll Along” ($1.3 million). Focus Features is releasing “Six,” which lands a few weekends after Bleecker Street’s “Hadestown” established an opening weekend record among Broadway live-captures with $10.2 million. “Hadestown” has been a surprise hit with $20 million domestically since late July.
	

	Elsewhere on box office charts, the Angel Studios historical drama “The Brink of War” opened in seventh place with $2.6 million from 2,083 theaters. Set during the Reykjavík Summit of 1986, the movie stars Jeff Daniels as Ronald Reagan as he races against time to salvage a deal with Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev (Jared Harris) to dismantle nuclear arsenals. Audiences liked the film, which secured an “A” grade on CinemaScore. 

	“This is a weak opening for a war drama,” Gross says. “Angel Studios knows how to get this audience to the theater, but this title is not getting Angel’s usual traction.”

	Another newcomer, Black Bear’s crime thriller “The Rivals of Amziah King,” starring Matthew McConaughey, earned a decent $1 million from just 632 theaters. The well-reviewed movie follows McConaughey as a honeymaker and born-again Christian whose former foster daughter reappears in his life. 

	Meanwhile, Universal’s R-rated comedy “One Night Only” failed to rebound, bringing in $2 million in its second weekend, a 61% decrease in ticket sales. The movie, which takes place during the one night a year when premarital sex is legal, has grossed $10 million against a $25 million budget.

schema.headline: Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Remains No. 1 With $70 Million, ‘End of Oak Street’ Debuts to $21 Million

title: Paul Mescal, Joseph Quinn, Barry Keoghan and Harris Dickinson Spotted Filming Beatles Biopic at Iconic Abbey Road Crosswalk
description:
It wouldn’t be a Beatles movie without Abbey Road.

	In a video shared on social media, Harris Dickinson, Paul Mescal, Joseph Quinn and Barry Keogha
body:
It wouldn’t be a Beatles movie without Abbey Road.

	In a video shared on social media, Harris Dickinson, Paul Mescal, Joseph Quinn and Barry Keoghan were shown recreating the iconic album cover for Sam Mendes’ multi-part Beatles biopic, titled “The Beatles – A Four-Film Cinematic Event.”


	Each film in the series will be from the perspective of a different band member, and all four films are set for an April 2028 release by Sony Pictures. Mendes’ project marks the first time that the Beatles and their estates have signed off on life rights and music for a theatrical feature film about them.
	

	Mescal stars as Paul McCartney, Quinn plays George Harrison, Barry Keoghan portrays Ringo Starr and Harris Dickinson plays John Lennon.


	Other cast members include Saoirse Ronan as Linda McCartney, James Norton as Brian Epstein, Mia McKenna-Bruce as Maureen Starkey, Anna Sawai as Yoko Ono, Aimee Lou Wood as Pattie Boyd, Harry Lloyd as George Martin, David Morrissey as Jim McCartney, Leanne Best as Mimi Smith, Bobby Schofield as Neil Aspinall, Daniel Hoffmann-Gill as Mal Evans, Arthur Darvill as Derek Taylor and Adam Pally as Allen Klein.

	The film’s official logline reads: “Each man has his own story, but together they are legendary.” During CinemaCon 2025, Mendes, who directs all four installments, described the project as the “first binge-able theatrical experience.” It is currently unknown if the films will be released all at once or once a week throughout April. Sony Pictures chief Tom Rothman added at the time that principal photography for the four films will take a year.

schema.headline: Paul Mescal, Joseph Quinn, Barry Keoghan and Harris Dickinson Spotted Filming Beatles Biopic at Iconic Abbey Road Crosswalk

title: Cristiano Ronaldo Plans to Retire After Marriage, Wants to Leave 'Spectacular' Legacy
description:
Cristiano Ronaldo
                          I'm Walking Away From Soccer After This Season
body:
Cristiano Ronaldo
                          I'm Walking Away From Soccer After This Season
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 16, 2026
                            11:45 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Cristiano Ronaldo is preparing to hang up his cleats ... revealing this will probably be his final year of soccer after a quarter-century on the pitch.
      
    
            The bombshell came almost as an aside during a joint Vogue interview with his new wife, Georgina Rodríguez. When the newlyweds were asked whether marriage would change anything, Ronaldo announced ... "This is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The 41-year-old superstar says he already has his post-soccer future mapped out ... acknowledging the game could leave a major hole in his life, but saying he plans to fill his time with family, travel, padel and simply enjoying everything he and Georgina have earned.
      

            As Ronaldo put it ... "After all it's been 25 years with a lot of sacrifice."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The five-time Ballon d'Or winner currently plays for Saudi club Al-Nassr and recently competed in his sixth and final World Cup for Portugal.
      
    
            Ronaldo and Georgina tied the knot Tuesday in an intimate ceremony inside their Portugal home, surrounded by their five children. There was no honeymoon -- Ronaldo had to head right back to Riyadh for the new season.
      
    
            One last run ... and CR7 wants to make it count.

title: President Trump Floats Fox News Reporter to Replace Karoline Leavitt
description:
President Trump
                          Maybe Fox News Has Karoline Leavitt's Replacement
body:
President Trump
                          Maybe Fox News Has Karoline Leavitt's Replacement
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 16, 2026
                            12:18 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            President Trump says Karoline Leavitt is irreplaceable ... though he may have found her successor standing on the other side of a Fox News microphone.
      
    
            During a Fox News interview, correspondent Alexis McAdams asked Trump whether Leavitt could be replaced. Trump said no, praised her work and joked he was concerned because "she likes her children more than she likes Trump."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            When McAdams pressed him on who he wanted behind the White House podium next, Trump turned the question right back on her -- "You? How about you?" -- before saying she could do the job.
      

            Trump even sought approval from Leavitt, who was standing nearby, then told McAdams he had always liked her and praised her work ... noting he doesn’t make offers like that very often.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Trump announced Wednesday that Leavitt will leave the role at the end of August to spend more time with her two young children.
      
    
            She'll remain one of Trump's top outside advisers.
      
    
            No official replacement has been announced ... but McAdams asked Trump whether he wanted to make news during their interview -- and she may have ended up becoming the news herself!
